Mariupol Old Jewish Cemetry

Jewish Cemetery · Donets'ka oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Mariupol's Jewish population reached 111 by 1847, though official settlement rights came only in 1859; the first synagogue, built in 1864, was destroyed during WWI. By 1897, the community had grown to 5,013 (16 percent), maintaining four synagogues, a hospital, and multiple schools by the 1910s, though pogroms struck in both 1905 and 1919. The community numbered 10,944 (5 percent) by 1939; after the German arrival in October 1941, about 8,000 Jews were murdered within days. The community revived after the war and again in the 1990s.
